rules_applied: Compact: keys kept in insertion order, no whitespace, UTF-8
JCS: object keys sorted in UTF-16 code-unit (Unicode code-point) order, not locale
JCS: 'C' (U+0043, 67) before 'a' (U+0061, 97) before 'b' (U+0062, 98) — code-unit order
Numbers: JSON number formatting unchanged (integer literals)
Compact: insertion order preserved at every nesting level, no whitespace
JCS: top-level keys sorted: 'outer'
JCS: nested object keys within 'outer' sorted: 'a' (U+0061), 'z' (U+007A)
JCS: object keys inside arrays are also sorted (arrays keep element order, but keys of objects they contain are canonicalized)
JCS: array element order unchanged: [{"x":2,"y":1},{"k":null}]
JCS: keys inside first array element sorted: 'x' before 'y' (U+0078 < U+0079)
JCS: 'k':null remains null
n1=1e21: JCS uses ECMAScript Number serialization — 1e21 is representable exactly, no + sign, written as '1e21'
n2=1e-7: smallest magnitude non-zero with no exact finite decimal; same form '1e-7' (no leading +)
n3=0.000001: exact binary representation, serialized as '0.000001' (decimal form, not exponential)
n4=100000000000000000000: large integer within safe range serialized as decimal integer with no exponential notation — '100000000000000000000'
n5=-0: JCS distinguishes -0 from +0; serialized as '-0.0' (minus sign preserved, with '.0')
n6=333333333.33333329: exact value representable, serialized as decimal '333333333.33333329' (no exponent)
Key sort: all keys 'n1'..'n6' already in order; JCS key sorting by UTF-16 code units: 'n1'<n2'<...<'n6'
JCS key sort uses UTF-16 code-unit (binary) comparison, NOT Unicode code-point or locale
Code-unit values of lead surrogates: '$' U+0024 (36), 'a' U+0061 (97), 'ü' U+00FC (252) — but in UTF-16 'ü' is one 16-bit code unit 0x00FC
€ (U+20AC) in UTF-16 is code unit 0x20AC (8396)
Order by UTF-16 code units: 0x0024 ('$') < 0x0061 ('a') < 0x00FC ('ü') < 0x20AC ('€')
Thus JCS order: '$', 'aa', 'ü', '€'
Compact kept insertion order: €, $, ü, aa
JCS strings use minimal escape per JSON/JavaScript: \n for U+000A, \t for U+0009, \" for U+0022
s1: line feed (U+000A) escaped as \n
s2: tab (U+0009) escaped as \t
s3: double quote (U+0022) escaped as \"
s4: 'é' (U+00E9) is a printable non-ASCII character — JCS does NOT escape it; kept as literal UTF-8 'é'

s5: trailing spaces — JCS does not escape regular space (U+0020); BUT a single trailing space before closing quote: if string ends with a space, JCS per RFC 8785 does NOT escape it — kept as literal space
Note: 'control  ' contains a trailing space only (U+0020), not a control character; no escaping needed
If string had U+0000 or other control chars (U+0000-U+001F except the escaped ones), they would be \uXXXX escaped
